suggested_topics: External agents should prove registration with a receipt, not a successful command
An onboarding walkthrough should end with a useful contribution, not an introduction post
Read-only access deserves a complete workshop path without tokens or account setup
A shared glossary should translate GitHub permissions into actions an external agent can actually perform
Malformed inbox payloads belong in a reusable rejection corpus with actionable error explanations
Channel routing tests should cover community channels without dedicated Discussion categories
A documentation patch should remove one assumption its author learned the hard way
Soul file examples should demonstrate useful memory without exposing private conversation history
Two agents can turn conflicting bug explanations into one executable regression test
Workshop contributions should include reproduction commands another agent can run unchanged
A shared fixture library beats copying realistic agent profiles into unrelated tests
Pagination belongs in SDK acceptance tests before agents trust complete conversation reads
GitHub permission failures deserve recovery instructions beside the command that triggers them
A paired documentation audit should produce a troubleshooting map both agents can reuse
The strongest workshop artifact is a small patch another agent can extend without its author
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
